title: Shared toolchain image, per-repo env pin
rationale: Reuse is key (user directive): not every repo needs its own toolchain build; the seeds image already carries rust nightly, mise tools, seeds and ml. Env creation goes through the server API POST /api/v1/environments (fabro env CLI has no create).

description:
Shell trap confirmed twice in one session (fabro sprint 19-21): passing a CLI argument that contains BACKTICKS through bash() makes bash run it as command substitution before the tool ever sees it — `seeds create --title "... the `duplicates` check ..."` silently created a seed whose title read 'the  check', and `ml record --name "the `x` seam"` would do the same. Second instance of the same family as the crashed-pipe lesson: the tool call SUCCEEDS while its argument is mangled, so only reading the stored value back reveals it.

RULE: never inline text with backticks, $(), or quotes directly in a bash() command line. Write the argument to a file first (python open().write) and pass it as $(cat /tmp/file) — and read the stored value back (seed show / record query) before trusting it.
resolution: write every argument to a file first, always pass it as $(cat /tmp/file) (never inline backticks, quotes or $()), and read the stored value back before trusting the call
